parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish عدالت (ʼadalet, “justice”), from Classical Persian عدالت, from Arabic عَدَالَةٌ f (ʕadālatun, verbal noun). Compare to Azerbaijani ədalət, Uyghur ئادالەت (adalet), Uzbek adolat.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish عینی (aynı, ayni, eyni), from Classical Persian عَیْنِی (aynī, “identical, same”), from Arabic عَيْنِيّ (ʕayniyy). By surface analysis, ayn + -i.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish بلبل (bülbül), itself from Classical Persian بُلْبُل (bulbul, “nightingale”), from Arabic بُلْبُل (bulbul)
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جاده (cadde), from Classical Persian جاده (jādda), from Arabic جَادَّة (jādda).

parole.significato: Jumada II (the sixth month of the Islamic calendar)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جمادی الآخر (cemaziyü'l-ahır, cemaziyelahir), from Classical Persian جَمَادِیُٱلْآخِر (jamādiyu-l-'āxir), from Arabic جُمَادَى ٱلْآخِر (jumādā l-ʔāḵir), ellipsis of شَهْر جُمَادَى ٱلْآخِر (šahr jumādā l-ʔāḵir).

parole.significato: Jumada I (the fifth month of the Islamic calendar)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جمادی الاول (cemaziyü'l-evvel, cemaziyelevvel), from Classical Persian جَمَادِیُٱلاَوَّل (jamādiyu-l-awwal), from Arabic جُمَادَى ٱلْأَوَّل (jumādā l-ʔawwal), ellipsis of شَهْر جُمَادَى ٱلْأَوَّل (šahr jumādā l-ʔawwal).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جنت, from Old Anatolian Turkish جَنَّت, borrowed from Classical Persian جَنَّت (jannat), borrowed from Arabic جَنَّة (janna). Compare Azerbaijani cənnət and Albanian xhenet.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جنت (cinnet), from Classical Persian جِنَّت (jinnat), from Arabic جِنَّة (jinna).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جُمْعَه (cüma, “Friday”), from Classical Persian جُمْعَه (jum'a, “Friday”), from Arabic الْجُمْعَةُ f (al-jumʕatu, “Friday”). Compare also Azerbaijani cümə, Uzbek juma, Kazakh жұма (juma), etc.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish دائمی (daimî), from Classical Persian دائمی (dā'imī / dâ'emi), a pseudo-Arabism from the root د و م (d w m).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish دینی (dīnī /⁠dīnī⁠/), from Classical Persian دینی (dīnī /⁠dīnī⁠/), from Arabic دِينِيّ m (dīniyy). By surface analysis, din (“religion”) + -i (nisba suffix). Compare also Azerbaijani dini, Kazakh діни (diniy), etc.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish امر (emr), from Old Anatolian Turkish امر (emr), from Classical Persian امر (amr), from Arabic أَمْر (ʔamr).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فلاكت (felaket), from Classical Persian فَلَاکَت (falākat), from Arabic فَلَاكَة (falāka).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فلج (felc, felç), from Classical Persian فَلَج (falaj), seemingly from verbal noun فَلَج (falaj) of passive-only base stem deverbal Arabic فُلِجَ (fulija) from فَالَج (fālaj), borrowed from Aramaic פָּלְגָּא / ܦܴܠܓܳܐ (pālgā), from Ancient Greek πλῆξις (plêxis), πληγή (

parole.significato: hazelnut, filbert, the nutlike fruit of the tree Corylus avellana
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فندق (funduk, fındık), borrowed from Classical Persian فُنْدُق (funduq), borrowed from Arabic فُنْدُق (funduq), borrowed from Middle Persian pndk' (pondik), borrowed from Ancient Greek Ποντικὸν κάρυον (Pontikòn káruon), from Ποντῐκόν (Pontĭkón) + κᾰ́ρῠον (kắrŭon).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish غرض (garaz, garez, “aim, goal; grudge”), from Classical Persian غرض (ġaraz, “spite, grudge, rancour”), from Arabic غَرَض (ḡaraḍ, “object of will; target”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish غیر (gayr-i), from Classical Persian غیرـ (ġayr-i-), from Arabic غَيْر (ḡayr) + Classical Persian ezafe. Cognate with Azerbaijani qeyri-, Uyghur غەيرى (gheyri), Uzbek gʻayri-.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish غازی, from Classical Persian غازی (ġāzī), from Arabic غَازٍ (ḡāzin).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish حرارت, from Old Anatolian Turkish حرارت, borrowed from Classical Persian حَرَارَت (harārat), borrowed from Arabic حَرَارَة (ḥarāra).

parole.significato: A title in the Ottoman Empire given to those who became a senior in a particular office.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خاصكی (hasseki, haseki, “(formerly) one of a body of sergeants-at-arms, sixty of whom formed the body guard of the Sultan; their officers that filled important public offices”), from Classical Persian خاصگی (xāssagī, xāsagī, “the favorite of the ruler”), from Arabic خَ

parole.significato: galangal, any of several plants of the genus Alpinia, especially Alpinia galanga
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خولنجان (havlincan), from Old Anatolian Turkish خولنجان (havlincan), from Classical Persian خولنجان (xawlenjân), from Arabic خَوْلَنْجَان (ḵawlanjān), from قولنجان (qulanjân, qulenjân), from Sanskrit कुलञ्जन (kulañjana), possibly from Chinese 高良薑／高良姜 (gāoliángjiāng).
From Ottoman Turkish حوضه (havza), from Classical Persian حوضه (havza), suffixed [Term?] + ـه (-a) from Arabic حَوْض (ḥawḍ).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خیر (hayr, hayır), ultimately shortened from Classical Persian نَخَیْر (naxayr, “no”), itself from نَه (na, “no”) + Arabic خَيْر (ḵayr, “good, well, wellbeing”). Partially replaced yok, although the latter is still more common.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish حاضر, from Classical Persian حَاضِر (hāzir), from Arabic حَاضِر (ḥāḍir).

parole.significato: halva, a traditional Middle Eastern confection usually made from crushed sesame seeds and honey
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish حلوا (helva, halva), from Classical Persian حَلْوَا (halwā, “sweetmeat”), from Arabic حَلْوَى (ḥalwā, “candy, confection, dessert”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish حكمران (hükümran), from Classical Persian حُکْمْرَانْ (hukmrān), from Arabic حُكْم (ḥukm).

parole.significato: synonym of iyi niyet (“good faith, good intentions”)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish حسن نیت (hüsn-i niyet), from Classical Persian حُسْنِ نِیَّت (husn-i niyyat), from Arabic حُسْنُ نِيَّةٍ (ḥusnu niyyatin, “good intentions”), from Arabic حُسْن (ḥusn, “beauty, fairness”) and نِيَّة (niyya, “intention, purpose”). By surface analysis, hüsn (“beauty”) + -
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اضافت (izafet), from Classical Persian اضافت (izâfat), itself from Arabic إِضَافَة (ʔiḍāfa). Doublet of izafe.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قلعه (kalʼa / kalʼe), قله (kale), from Classical Persian قلعه (qal'a), from Arabic قَلْعَةٌ (qalʕatun, “fort; fortress”). Compare also Azerbaijani qala, Uzbek qalʼa, Kazakh қала (qala), etc.

parole.significato: pen, pencil, or any similar writing tool
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قلم (kalem), from Old Anatolian Turkish قَلَمۡ (qalem), borrowed from Classical Persian قَلَم (qalam), borrowed from Arabic قَلَم (qalam), from Ancient Greek κάλαμος (kálamos), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱélh₂m̥ (“reed, straw”). Doublet of kalamar.

parole.significato: A public weighing machine of the Ottoman era, or the office where the machine was located.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قپان (kapan), from Old Anatolian Turkish قپان, borrowed from Classical Persian قپان (qapān, qappān), from Arabic قبان (qabbān), from Byzantine Greek κάμπανος (kámpanos), γάμπανος (gámpanos), from Latin campāna.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كریم (kerim), from Classical Persian کریم (karīm), from Arabic كَرِيمُ (karīmu, “noble”, adjective).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ماجرا (macera), from Classical Persian مَاجَرَا (mājarā), from Arabic مَا جَرَى (mā jarā, literally “what happened”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish محبت (muhabbet), from Classical Persian مُحَبَّت (muhabbat), from Arabic مَحَبَّة (maḥabba, “love”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish موسیقی (musiki), from Classical Persian موسیقی (musīqī), from Arabic مُوسِيقَى (mūsīqā), from Ancient Greek μουσική (mousikḗ). Doublet of müzik and mızıka.
From Ottoman Turkish مسلمان (müslimân), from Classical Persian مُسَلْمَان (musalmān, “Muslim”), from Arabic مُسْلِم (muslim, “Muslim”).

parole.significato: rival, competitor, opponent, contender, adversary, a person or organization against whom one is competing
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish رقیب (rakib, “rival, competitor”), from Classical Persian رقیب (raqīb, “rival, competitor”), from Arabic رَقِيب (raqīb, “watchman, guard, sentry”).

parole.significato: Ramadan (the holy ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, during which Muslims fast between the break of dawn until…
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish رمضان (ramazân), from Classical Persian رمضان (ramazān), from Arabic رَمَضَان (ramaḍān).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish رَبَاب (rebâp), from Classical Persian رُبَاب (rubāb), from Arabic رُبَاب (rubāb), plural of رَبَابَة (rabāba).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish رقابت (rekâbet, “rivalry, competition”), from Classical Persian رقابت (rakabat), from Arabic رَقَابَة (raqāba).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish رشوت (rişvet, rüşvet, “bribe”), from Classical Persian رِشْوَه (rišwa), from Arabic رِشْوَة (rišwa).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish صلاحیت (salâhiyet, “goodness, fitness, ability; authority”), from Classical Persian صلاحیت (salāhiyat), from Arabic صَلَاحِيَّةٌ f (ṣalāḥiyyatun). See also Persian صلاحیت (salâhiyat, “authority”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سطرنج (satranc), itself from Classical Persian or Arabic شَطْرَنْج (šaṭranj), ultimately from Sanskrit चतुरङ्ग (caturaṅga).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سفالت (sefâlet), from Classical Persian سَفَالَت (safālat), from Arabic سَفَالَة (safāla).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سیر و سفر (seyr ü sefer), from Classical Persian سیر و سفر (sayr u safar, “travel”), from Arabic سَيْر (sayr, “movement, traffic”) and Arabic سَفَر (safar, “travel”). By surface analysis, seyir + ü + sefer.

parole.significato: hyacinth, any bulbous flowering plant of the genus Hyacinthus
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سنبل (sünbül), from Classical Persian سنبل (sunbul, “hyacinth”), ultimately from Arabic سُنْبُل (sunbul, “kind of aromatic plant”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish دف (tef), from Classical Persian دف (daf), from Arabic دف (daff).

parole.significato: salaam, a low bow used as a ceremonial act of deference
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تمنا (temenna, “salaam”), from Classical Persian تمنا (tamannā, “wish, desire; entreaty, request”), from Arabic تَمَنَّى (tamannā, “to wish for, to desire”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تنقید (tenkid), from Classical Persian تَنْقِید (tanqīd), a pseudo-Arabism from the root ن ق د (n q d).

parole.significato: black francolin, any game bird of the species Francolinus francolinus, native to south and southwestern Asia
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تراج (turac, “black francolin”), from Classical Persian تراج (torrâj), ultimately from Arabic دُرَّاج (durrāj, “francolin”).

Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish ظَالِم (zalım), from Classical Persian ظَالِم (zālim), from Arabic ظَالِم (ẓālim). Cognate with Gagauz zulum, Azerbaijani zalım and zalim. Used in Turkish since the 14th century.

parole.significato: lily, any of several flowering plants in the genus Lilium
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زنبق (zambak), from Classical Persian زنبق (zanbaq), from Arabic زَنْبَق (zanbaq), from Middle Persian [script needed] (cmbk' /⁠čambak⁠/), from Sanskrit चम्पक (campaka).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اِضْطِرَاب (ıztırâb), from Classical Persian اِضْطِرَاب (iztirāb), from Arabic اِضْطِرَاب (iḍṭirāb, “disturbance; disorder”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شربت (şerbet), borrowed from Classical Persian شَرْبَت (šarbat), borrowed from Arabic شَرْبَة (šarba), from شَرِبَ (šariba).
